summary.headline: City Union Bank Q4 FY26: advances up 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore and PAT up 25% to INR360 crore, with gross NPA at 1.91%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the bank's strongest quarter in recent years, with total business growing about 24% YoY and advances up 26% to INR66,698 crore. Asset quality kept improving: gross NPA fell to 1.91% from 3.09% a year earlier, and total SMA fell to 2.47% from 3.68% in Q3. Q4 PAT rose 25% to INR360 crore, the highest single quarter, and FY26 PAT rose 18% to INR1,326 crore with ROA at 1.56%. The call also marked the handover of MD and CEO from Dr. N. Kamakodi to R. Vijay Anandh effective 1 May 2026.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loans are about 30% of the book and growing faster than overall loans; management says the 30% level is near the upper limit, with 1-2% flexibility. Per-gram lending was capped around INR10,000-10,500 even at peak gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Core focus segment, with management citing rising capacity utilisation and CC limit usage as demand drivers. FY27 plan keeps MSME at 55-60% of the mix. Only 3-4% of MSME loans are under CGTMSE cover.

segments.name: Secured retail
segments.commentary: Housing and loans against property are growing and are an additional growth driver. FY27 plan uses secured retail to fill the remaining share of the mix after MSME and gold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth planned at 2-3% above industry credit growth, with MSME at 55-60%, gold loans and secured retail as additional enhancers.
FY27 NIM expected to stay in a narrow 5-10 bps band around the FY26 level of 3.74%.
FY27 operating expenses expected to rise 15-18% YoY, with about 75 branches to be opened in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end).
ROA to exit FY27 at least 10 bps higher, at about 1.65-1.67%, supported by retail income and lower cost-to-income.
CD ratio to be kept at 85-87%. Third-party business to be 1-2% of the book. Fee income to be 55-60% of other income.

Credit cost expected to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60% over the next 15 years; individual years may vary. Management said the ECL circular lets banks adjust the opening balance, so the ECL impact on P&L is expected to be limited.
capex_capacity: Branch network reached 1,000 with the opening of the 1,000th branch at Kumbakonam on 4 May 2026, up from about 950 at FY26 end.
About 75 branches to be opened in FY27, with about 50 in April 2026 (70 opened in the first month per the CEO-designate); branches typically reach breakeven in year one.
Distribution capacity was lifted by the Newgen LOS and digital process set, which the management credits for secured MSME and retail growth.
demand_pricing: Advances grew by over INR5,800 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR13,600 crore for the full year; double-digit growth has run for eight consecutive quarters.
Deposit growth was matched to credit growth, with CASA at 28% of deposits and the average CD ratio at 85% for FY26. Some CDs were replaced by retail term deposits.
Yield on advances was 9.80% in Q4 (9.73% in Q3) and 9.75% for FY26 (9.79% in FY25). The cost of deposits was 5.60% in Q4 (5.57% in Q3).
Management said rate passthrough was completed around December 2025, and incremental yields are holding up, with non-agri gold loans at double-digit yields.
Management is watching the US-Iran conflict and oil prices; no visible impact on asset quality so far. Management expects a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: How does the bank manage risk on gold loans given a 10-15% gold price fall from the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-gram lending was capped at about INR10,000-10,500 even when gold peaked at INR15,000-16,000, so there is a cushion. It cited a loss of about INR5 crore in the 2014 gold price crash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise 3 bps QoQ, and where will it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some deposit rates were fine-tuned by 10-25 bps to support fast credit growth. It said the 3-5 bps movement is noise from CASA rate variation and it can add INR3,000 crore of advances without new deposits.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield on advances keep falling after the rate cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate passthrough is complete, and roughly 30% of the book is fixed-rate gold. Incremental book of about INR5,000 crore booked in H2 was at higher yields, which held the margin.

qa_highlights.question: When does ROA move to 1.7-1.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO-designate said FY27 exit ROA should be 1.65-1.67%, at least 10 bps above the FY26 level, based on retail income and lower cost-to-income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for steady-state credit costs after the ECL norms?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the 15-year average credit cost is about 0.60%, and FY25 and FY26 were 0.09% and 0.04%. He expects at least a 50% reduction over the long run, with AI-based underwriting cited as the reason.

qa_highlights.question: Will underwriting filters tighten given fuel prices and demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it watches SMA trends and branch and customer feedback. It would add some caution to filters but has no plan to change them now, as underwriting is set for multiple business cycles.

risks_watch: Gold price correction on the INR30%+ gold book and whether LTV cushions hold.
Impact of the US-Iran conflict and oil prices on MSME demand and slippages; management expects an extra 1-2% slippage in a downturn.
Rising deposit costs as the bank fine-tunes rates to fund faster credit growth; the CD ratio is at 85% and CASA at 28%.
Opex growth of 15-18% in FY27 from branch expansion, against the ROA target of 1.65-1.67%.
Leadership transition: MD and CEO handover on 1 May 2026, plus the retirement of two independent directors in February 2026. The retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and asset quality, with management saying it met all earlier guidance. More cautious on macro risks, particularly the US-Iran conflict and fuel prices. Evasive on the ECL steady-state credit cost, deferring that question to the CEO-designate.
key_quotes: By and large, almost all the expectations whatever we shared with you in the earlier con-calls for the financial year 2026 were met in the same spirit whatever we had shared with you.
The gross NPA has come below 2 % mark after 11 years.
I think we should exit this year with at least 10 bps more in ROA, so we should be there between 1.65% to 1.67%.

adds.what: About 75 branches to be opened in FY27 (about 50 in April 2026, 25 by year-end); network reached 1,000 branches

growth.why: FY27 advances guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth, with opex up 15-18% and about 75 branches to open, backed by the 1,000-branch network and the Newgen LOS digital set-up, but no order-style or capacity-level numbers beyond branch counts.

mgmt.note: Dr. N. Kamakodi handed over MD and CEO role to R. Vijay Anandh effective 1 May 2026; the call did not give a detailed personal growth plan beyond FY27 guidance.
initiatives: Continue MSME focus at 55-60% of mix
Grow gold loans and secured retail as enhancers

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM is guided to stay within a narrow 5-10 bps band around FY26's 3.74%, and cost of deposits rose to 5.60% in Q4 from 5.57% in Q3 as rates were fine-tuned to fund credit growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network reached 1,000 after the Kumbakonam opening on 4 May 2026, with about 75 more branches planned in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end), a 7.9% addition to the network.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management plans advances growth 2-3% above industry credit growth, following 26% YoY in Q4 and INR13,600 crore added in FY26, with MSME at 55-60% of the mix and gold and secured retail as enhancers.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Advances grew 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore against FY27 guidance of only 2-3% above industry credit growth, and gross NPA fell to 1.91%, so the guide looks conservative if growth holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Opex is guided up 15-18% in FY27 against an ROA exit target of 1.65-1.67%, and management flags a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn tied to the US-Iran conflict and oil prices.

rows.label: Credit cost to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60%
rows.when: over the next 15 years, individual years may vary
rows.why: FY25 and FY26 credit costs were 0.09% and 0.04%, and management cites AI-based underwriting, but the long-run timing is uncertain and the CEO deferred on steady-state ECL questions.

rows.label: Gold loan price correction risk
rows.why: Gold is about 30% of the book with per-gram lending capped near INR10,000-10,500 versus a peak of INR15,000-16,000, and a 10-15% fall would be cushioned by LTV headroom.

rows.label: CEO handover to R. Vijay Anandh
rows.why: Leadership changed on 1 May 2026, and the retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, asset quality and branch expansion, but cautious on the US-Iran conflict and fuel prices and evasive on steady-state ECL credit costs, which it deferred to the CEO-designate.
